items.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015
items.q: my uncle sent me a double album set of Tommy Dorsey’s big band. He said if you play trombone you should know who Tommy Dorsey is. So I listened to that

ctx.x: Because it’s an interesting time for a young man. Did you have these aspirations then?

I loved music and I loved the trombone and I loved just the social aspect of the band, but I also loved the fact that it was something that I did pretty well and I felt like it was something that would get me out of my shell a little bit. And I started messing around with writing a little bit. I had — my uncle sent me a double album set of Tommy Dorsey’s big band. He said if you play trombone you should know who Tommy Dorsey is. So I listened to that, and tried to transcribe one of the charts, and this was in…

off an LP. So you can imagine what it did to the record. But that was a learning experience. And then — so it kind of started around that time believe it or not, like seventh or eighth grade where I was thinking this is a lot of fun, I wish I could do this all the time. I didn’t know you could actually do it, but I was hoping that there was some way I could continue playing that kind of music.
